record.paper_title: Open questions and perspectives for hadron electromagnetic form factors in space-like and time-like regions.
record.context_brief: Possible subthreshold nucleon-antinucleon resonance explaining time-like form factors
record.original_question: Are nucleon electromagnetic form factors systematically larger in the time-like region than in the space-like region because of a narrow nucleon-antinucleon resonance located just below the nucleon-antinucleon threshold?

evidence.quote: A possible explanation of the fact that FFs are systematically larger in TL region than in SL region (which is true also in the proton case) is the presence of a narrow resonance in the NN system, just below the NN threshold [19].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G_E^N(q^2)$ and $G_M^N(q^2)$ denote the Sachs electric and magnetic electromagnetic form factors of a nucleon $N$ (proton or neutron), considered as analytic functions of the squared four-momentum transfer $q^2$. For space-like momentum transfer ($q^2 < 0$), these form factors are measured in elastic electron–nucleon scattering. For time-like momentum transfer ($q^2 \ge 4 m_N^2$, where $m_N$ is the nucleon mass), they are accessed through reactions such as $e^+ e^- \leftrightarrow N \bar N$. Empirical data indicate that, when compared at $|q^2|$ values of comparable magnitude, the moduli $|G^N(q^2)|$ in the time-like region are systematically larger than the corresponding values in the space-like region.

Determine whether this systematic enhancement of the time-like nucleon electromagnetic form factors relative to their space-like counterparts can be explained by the existence of a narrow resonance in the nucleon–antinucleon ($N\bar N$) system located just below the $N\bar N$ production threshold $q^2 = 4 m_N^2$. Specifically: does such a narrow subthreshold $N\bar N$ resonance exist, and if so, does it quantitatively account for the observed space-like/time-like asymmetry of $G_E^N$ and $G_M^N$?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (through 2024–2025) on nucleon electromagnetic form factors continues to discuss the enhancement of time-like form factors over space-like ones and proposes a possible narrow $N\bar N$ subthreshold resonance as one explanation, alongside competing accounts based on final-state $N\bar N$ interactions (e.g., chiral EFT distorted-wave Born approximation) and extended vector-meson-dominance models with oscillatory structures. No definitive experimental confirmation of such a narrow subthreshold resonance has been established, and dispersion-theoretical analyses still list this as an open question requiring dedicated threshold-region measurements.

status_evidence.title: Nucleon form factors stride into the future – CERN Courier
status_evidence.snippet: Time-like form factors are roughly twice as large as space-like ones; a possible N̄N resonance below threshold is invoked as one explanation.
status_evidence.claim: The space-like/time-like enhancement is still discussed as an open puzzle with a possible subthreshold N̄N resonance as one candidate explanation.

status_evidence.title: Dispersion-theoretical analysis of the electromagnetic form factors of the nucleon: Past, present and future
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses near-threshold behavior and possible resonance structures slightly below the N̄N threshold within dispersion analyses.
status_evidence.claim: Dispersion analyses still treat the subthreshold resonance hypothesis as unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Study of the electromagnetic form factors of the nucleons in the timelike region
status_evidence.snippet: Models the time-like enhancement via N̄N final-state interactions in chiral EFT rather than a narrow subthreshold resonance.
status_evidence.claim: Competing explanations (final-state interactions) remain viable, so the resonance interpretation is not confirmed.
